title: Arquitectura, DDD y decisiones técnicas
scope: LESSONS_ONLY: title/tagline/job relevance, 8 outcomes, 34/34 theory/reference paragraphs, 9 theory code/output blocks, 10 callouts, 2 declared figures and 1 Theory playground. I Do / We Do / You Do / self-check / exams excluded.

research_basis.use: Bounded contexts can share concepts and use different local models; mappings between contexts matter. Disjoint vocabulary tokens are not a DDD invariant.
C4 container means an application or data store, not Docker; context/container are valid abstractions but level-name presence is not a diagram.
Container diagrams show responsibilities, technology choices and communication between containers.
Original ADR structure is title/status/context/decision/consequences; rollback and alternatives are useful local/MADR additions, not universal original ADR requirements.
MADR explicitly adds considered options/trade-off information; distinguishes template choices from Nygard core.
SemVer requires a declared precise public API before version numbers communicate compatibility.
Services must explicitly define breaking-change/extensibility policy; adding response fields is safe only under compatible client rules, and different Microsoft services define this differently.
Even in an evolvable API, only qualified additions are nonbreaking; new required fields, non-evolvable enum members, behavior/performance changes can break clients.
Complex material benefits from learner-paced segmentation; figures should be spatially contiguous with the concept they explain.

rejected_findings.evidence: Official C4 guidance treats context and container diagrams as high-value core views; the defect is that S40 validates only their names, not diagram contents/relationships.
Official C4 says container is an application or data store; S40 examples api/worker/db/object_store are conceptually appropriate.

rejected_findings.claim: Infrastructure depending inward on a domain port is always inverted.
rejected_findings.evidence: Ports/adapters deliberately makes outer adapters depend on inner abstractions; S40's basic arrow direction is defensible.

rejected_findings.claim: An ADR may never include alternatives or rollback.
rejected_findings.evidence: MADR and local governance rubrics can legitimately include them. The defect is presenting the local rubric as if it were the universal ADR definition.

rejected_findings.claim: Every added response field is necessarily breaking.
rejected_findings.evidence: Compatibility depends on the declared extensibility policy and client behavior. S40's defect is the opposite absolute: it says additive means compatible without declaring those rules.

rejected_findings.claim: The architecture-ddd-decisions id should be renamed now.
rejected_findings.evidence: It is a stable URL/progress key and currently describes the topic reasonably well; migration risk outweighs cosmetic cleanup.

rejected_findings.claim: The source incorrectly says a value object is often immutable.
rejected_findings.evidence: That conceptual statement is standard and the prose explicitly admits vo_frozen=True does not freeze a Python dict. The narrower evidence-quality problem remains captured separately.

rejected_findings.claim: The no-agent scope paragraph is itself wrong.
rejected_findings.evidence: The scope choice is coherent; the defect is the shared Theory playground that violates it.

findings.summary: Opening says S39 closed triage with controls/evidence and the system works, while the current audit continuation says S39 REPAIR_REQUIRED and CF-3 blocked.
findings.attack: Phase-3 architecture begins by laundering unresolved N3 evidence into a working-system premise.
findings.defense: S40 needs a narrative bridge from S39.
findings.fix: State that S39 produced provisional artifacts with open defects; architecture must not promote them until repaired gates are linked.

findings.summary: Architecture dossier names stages but does not bind boundaries/interfaces to immutable artifact IDs, hashes, versions or contract-test evidence from S39.
findings.attack: A diagram can be internally tidy while referring to stale model, graph, feature, policy or decision artifacts.
findings.defense: S40 is intentionally stdlib/conceptual.
findings.fix: Require an architecture manifest mapping every context/interface to artifact/version/hash/as-of and contract-test IDs.

findings.summary: S39 governance interfaces—human decision/override, appeal, feedback eligibility, drift events, rollback bundle and no-autofraud policy—are absent from S40's boundary model.
findings.attack: Context separation can erase the cross-cutting traceability CF-3 requires.
findings.defense: S40 focuses on architecture concepts rather than reproducing every S39 detail.
findings.fix: Represent governance as explicit interfaces/policies crossing contexts, with IDs and ownership, rather than omitting them.

findings.summary: s40_map_contract.py returns gate names and literal booleans instead of evaluating architecture evidence.
findings.attack: agent_orchestration_topic=False and pii_allowed=False prove nothing about rendered content or data flow.
findings.defense: Reference block says names explain criteria rather than asking learners to memorize them.
findings.fix: Compute gate results from actual manifest/graph/contract artifacts; keep labels separate from evidence.

findings.summary: Theory playground is a Researcher/Analyst/Writer multi-agent simulation even though S40 explicitly excludes agent orchestration.
findings.attack: Learner practices the exact topic the section says is out of scope.
findings.defense: The stable id is historical and the playground likely predates the rewrite.
findings.fix: Preserve id but replace mapping with architecture/DDD decision playground.

findings.summary: Tagline promises separation of intake, ER, relationship, triage, reporting and AI, while Theory's executable context-map contract only models intake and ER.
findings.attack: Learner-facing headline overstates demonstrated breadth.
findings.defense: The You Do later expands the map, but it is outside this lesson-only theory evidence.
findings.fix: Teach at least the full boundary/interface skeleton in Theory or narrow the tagline to what Theory demonstrates.

findings.summary: Job relevance says this documentation is what a technical committee accepts before approving a serious project, phrased as a universal fact.
findings.attack: Architecture governance varies by organization; C4/ADR dossiers are useful practices, not universal approval prerequisites.
findings.defense: It is motivational shorthand for professional relevance.
findings.fix: Use scoped language: 'puede formar parte de la evidencia que un comité técnico revisa'.

findings.summary: The p95/100 req/s scenario is handwritten and qa_complete never computes p95 or binds it to benchmark samples/environment.
findings.attack: S37 measurement debt is silently converted into valid architecture evidence.
findings.defense: S40 is about scenario structure rather than load-testing mechanics.
findings.fix: Reference a BenchmarkResult/manifest and distinguish target from measured evidence.

findings.summary: qa_complete validates key presence but empty source/stimulus/environment/response/owner still passes.
findings.attack: CE01 produces complete=True without an owner or meaningful scenario.
findings.defense: The happy-path fixture uses populated fields.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty normalized text and owner identity against an ownership registry.

findings.summary: qa_complete accepts booleans, negative times and infinite targets.
findings.attack: CE02–CE04 turn impossible telemetry into valid evidence.
findings.defense: Typed educational fixtures are intended.
findings.fix: Reject bool/non-numeric/non-finite/negative values and require observed measure semantics.

findings.summary: Owner is a free-form string such as platform/arquitectura despite outcomes requiring a contactable owner and residual acceptance.
findings.attack: No actor ID, role, approval event, timestamp or escalation path exists.
findings.defense: Human directory integration is outside stdlib scope.
findings.fix: Use synthetic owner_id plus approval metadata and contact/escalation reference; no external directory required.

findings.summary: T1-A declares S40-layer-imports, but it is absent from bespoke FIGURES and all FIGURE_DATA registries; FigureFrame therefore returns null.
findings.attack: Declared instructional figure is invisible.
findings.defense: Caption text remains in source but FigureFrame intentionally returns null for unknown IDs.
findings.fix: Register the figure or replace with an existing valid ID and test rendering.

findings.summary: S40-layer-imports describes layers/framework imports but is attached to T1-A quality attributes rather than T2-A layers.
findings.attack: Even after renderer repair, the diagram is separated from the concept it explains, increasing split attention.
findings.defense: It previews a later architectural concern.
findings.fix: Move it to T2-A and use a QA-scenario figure in T1-A if needed.

findings.summary: Registered S40-ports-adapters is attached to T1-B trade-offs instead of T2-B ports/adapters.
findings.attack: The only ports/adapters visual appears before and away from its matching explanation.
findings.defense: It can serve as an example decision alternative.
findings.fix: Move the figure to T2-B; keep T1-B focused on criteria/risk.

findings.summary: Theory calls 3.8/2.2 weighted-cost scores but defines no criteria, weights, raw values or calculation.
findings.attack: Decision table becomes an unexplained magic number ranking.
findings.defense: The lab emphasizes min-cost direction rather than MCDA mechanics.
findings.fix: Expose criterion, weight, normalized value and contribution or stop calling the values weighted scores.

findings.summary: Prose defines residual risk as probability×impact with mitigation, but choose_option receives one scalar residual_ok only.
findings.attack: Probability, impact, mitigation and residual rationale can all be absent while gate passes.
findings.defense: Scalar simplifies the lab.
findings.fix: Represent risk record with likelihood, impact, mitigation, residual value, threshold and evidence.

findings.summary: Outcome/callout require an owner to accept residual risk, but choose_option has no owner or acceptance event.
findings.attack: A critical governance requirement exists only in prose.
findings.defense: Fixture paragraph names arquitectura.
findings.fix: Require owner_id and signed/recorded acceptance in the decision artifact.

findings.summary: choose_option crashes on empty options, accepts negative residual, can select NaN by ordering and collapses duplicate names in the scores dict.
findings.attack: CE05–CE08 make invalid decision evidence look valid or non-deterministic.
findings.defense: Happy-path options are clean.
findings.fix: Validate non-empty unique alternatives, finite scores, residual domain and deterministic tie policy.

findings.summary: deps_ok([]), unknown layer names and dependency cycles all pass.
findings.attack: CE09–CE11 show absence/corruption of architecture evidence is green.
findings.defense: The helper only illustrates two prohibited edges.
findings.fix: Validate node vocabulary, required layers, non-empty evidence, cycles and permitted dependency rules.

findings.summary: Two exact forbidden edges cannot prove dependency inversion, transitive boundaries or port ownership.
findings.attack: The validator can approve arbitrary edges it has never defined.
findings.defense: A compact blacklist makes the core examples memorable.
findings.fix: Use an explicit architecture policy/allowlist with graph semantics and contract edges.

findings.summary: Theory promises implements_port, empty domain imports and ≥3 contract tests, but code runs one happy MemoryCaseRepo call and prints port_ok=True.
findings.attack: No contract tests or import evidence exist.
findings.defense: Protocol type hint demonstrates dependency direction.
findings.fix: Run a shared contract suite against at least memory and one alternate fake/adapter; inspect/import-boundary evidence separately.

findings.summary: Text says SQL adapter can replace memory without rewriting business rule, but no second adapter or failure behavior is tested.
findings.attack: Structural shape alone does not prove semantic substitutability.
findings.defense: The section intentionally avoids SQL dependency.
findings.fix: Add a second stdlib fake adapter with the same contract, including not-found/error semantics.

findings.summary: Lab makes token-set disjointness a bounded-context promotion rule even though DDD contexts may share the same term with different local models.
findings.attack: Fowler explicitly notes products/customers can be common concepts across contexts; mapping handles polysemy. CE12 rejects a legitimate mapped overlap.
findings.defense: Source labels disjointness as a didactic simplification.
findings.fix: Validate local definition/ownership and explicit translation; never require vocabulary tokens themselves to be disjoint.

findings.summary: contexts_ok hard-codes only intake/ER and case→record; it does not model relation type, direction, ownership, version or other promised contexts.
findings.attack: A one-pair dict is not the context map described by the outcome/tagline.
findings.defense: It is a minimal first example.
findings.fix: Represent context nodes and typed directional relationships/translations across the promised contexts.

findings.summary: Boundaries carry words but not S39 node/edge/source evidence IDs, artifact versions, graph snapshot or as-of.
findings.attack: Translation can preserve terminology while losing investigative provenance.
findings.defense: DDD lesson focuses on language boundaries.
findings.fix: Define interface envelopes that retain evidence/provenance fields through translations.

findings.summary: vo_frozen=True remains a literal checklist rather than an executable immutable value object, despite the outcome promising testable invariants.
findings.attack: The code cannot detect mutation and therefore cannot substantiate the invariant.
findings.defense: The prose explicitly warns the flag does not freeze a dict and points to frozen dataclass/NamedTuple in production.
findings.fix: Use a frozen dataclass/NamedTuple in Theory so the stated invariant is actually executable.

findings.summary: merge_scores accepts non-finite/out-of-range scores and weights outside [0,1].
findings.attack: CE14–CE15 can emit values outside the triage score contract inherited from S39.
findings.defense: It illustrates a stateless service, not model validation.
findings.fix: Validate finite score/weight domains or use a non-risk example that cannot contaminate triage semantics.

findings.summary: adr_ready treats {'context','container'} as sufficient C4 evidence without people, systems, containers, responsibilities or relationships.
findings.attack: A set of level names can green the gate while no architecture map exists.
findings.defense: The source separately narrates example elements.
findings.fix: Validate actual C4 model records and relationships; level presence is only schema, not evidence.

findings.summary: Opening/T4-A describe alternatives and rollback as if every ADR definition requires them.
findings.attack: Nygard core ADR fields are status/context/decision/consequences; MADR and local governance templates add considered options. Rollback is valuable but local.
findings.defense: S40 deliberately uses a stricter governance rubric.
findings.fix: Say 'en la rúbrica de S40 añadimos alternatives y rollback' and distinguish it from the ADR concept.

findings.summary: adr_ready validates field-name membership and accepted string, not content quality.
findings.attack: CE16 passes an empty semantic ADR containing only labels.
findings.defense: T4-A paragraph later gives a richer five-part rubric.
findings.fix: Make the code enforce non-empty context, ≥2 alternatives, balanced consequences/residual, executable rollback and decision content.

findings.summary: status='accepted' is not tied to the contactable owner/signature the prose requires.
findings.attack: Any caller can type accepted and pass.
findings.defense: Owner verification is organizational metadata outside the minimal function.
findings.fix: Require decision_owner, accepted_by, accepted_at and review/reference IDs in the ADR record.

findings.summary: feature_flag_off is presented as rollback without compatibility, data-state or release-bundle evidence.
findings.attack: Turning off async flow may not reverse messages already emitted or schema/policy changes.
findings.defense: It is an illustrative rollback signal.
findings.fix: Define rollback preconditions, version bundle, verification test and irreversible side effects.

findings.summary: Theory says compatible changes are additive and adding fields/events preserves old consumers.
findings.attack: Compatibility depends on explicit contract/extensibility rules; strict clients can reject unknown fields and behavioral changes can break without field deletion.
findings.defense: The example consumer intentionally ignores priority.
findings.fix: Teach compatibility relative to a declared public contract and tolerant-reader/extensibility policy.

findings.summary: No API policy says whether clients must ignore unknown response fields, enums are evolvable, ordering is contractual, or new fields may be required.
findings.attack: Microsoft guidelines explicitly require services to define breaking-change rules because different services make different choices.
findings.defense: S41 will implement the API.
findings.fix: S40 should define the compatibility policy S41 will implement before calling changes safe.

findings.summary: additive_ok compares one concrete v1 dict to one v_next dict and length.
findings.attack: CE17 cannot detect schema optionality/types/enums/behavior or other consumers.
findings.defense: consumer_view demonstrates one old reader survives the example.
findings.fix: Define schema/behavior contract fixtures and run old consumer contract tests against candidate versions.

findings.summary: Versioning language is used without declaring the public API and compatibility surface first.
findings.attack: SemVer explicitly requires a precise public API before version numbers can encode compatibility.
findings.defense: S40 does not explicitly claim full SemVer compliance.
findings.fix: Define public contract/schemas/events and compatibility rules before version increments or compatibility claims.

findings.summary: 'Versiona eventos (case.created) al cambiar semántica' gives no event schema/version field, migration strategy or consumer compatibility rule.
findings.attack: A stable event name does not itself version changed semantics.
findings.defense: It is a forward-looking reminder before S41+.
findings.fix: Show explicit event schema version/evolution rule and consumer contract.

findings.summary: Outcome/callout require debt owner and retire_on, but Theory executable never consumes either field.
findings.attack: The printed compatibility result can be green with no technical-debt governance at all.
findings.defense: The paragraph's example names platform and 2026-12-01.
findings.fix: Include debt record in the executable contract with owner identity, retirement condition/date and review status.

findings.summary: A single retire_on date substitutes for consumer inventory, support status, deprecation notice and removal criteria.
findings.attack: API evolution needs an upgrade/deprecation path, not only a future date.
findings.defense: S40 only introduces debt governance, not full lifecycle operations.
findings.fix: At minimum define affected consumers, support status, migration path and earliest removal condition.

findings.summary: No Theory code is a collected pytest suite despite the roadmap's systematic pytest requirement from S27.
findings.attack: All runtime false greens discovered here can regress without blocking CI.
findings.defense: S40 examples are short stdlib snippets.
findings.fix: Convert architecture validators and compatibility contracts into collected tests, including adversarial cases.

findings.summary: Theory repeats that ER does not imply fraud/relationship and review remains human, but architecture provides no explicit policy/interface preventing score or graph evidence from becoming a verdict across contexts.
findings.attack: The critical N3 safety invariant can disappear at the architecture boundary while prose stays correct.
findings.defense: S40 is not a triage-policy lesson.
findings.fix: Represent no-autofraud/abstention/human-decision policy as a named versioned boundary contract inherited from S39.

USABLE: Bounded contexts use local language/models and explicit mappings between contexts.
Ports/adapters can make outer adapters depend on inner ports while domain rules remain framework-independent.
C4 context and container are useful core views; C4 container means application/data store, not Docker.
Entities are tracked by identity and value objects compare by value; immutable VOs are a useful tactical pattern.
Architecture decisions should record context, decision and consequences; local governance may add alternatives, owner and rollback.
API compatibility must be reasoned about relative to a declared consumer/public contract, not aesthetics.
PARTIAL: Quality-attribute scenario validation and benchmark provenance.
Weighted trade-off computation and residual-risk acceptance.
Context-map relationship/translation model across all promised contexts.
Cross-context evidence lineage and N3 governance interfaces.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: S39 is closed and its system works.
Key presence equals a complete quality-attribute scenario.
A free-form owner string equals a contactable accountable owner.
Two handwritten scores equal a weighted decision model.
Residual risk is one unvalidated integer.
A two-edge blacklist proves clean architecture.
Bounded contexts should use disjoint vocabulary tokens.
vo_frozen=True makes a value object immutable.
A set containing context/container is a C4 diagram.
An ADR universally requires rollback and alternatives.
Adding a field is always backward compatible.
One payload instance equals a consumer contract.
case.created is versioned merely because prose says to version it.
A compatibility print proves debt owner/retirement governance.
